description: Server-side rendering of the Svelte 5 data grid. In SvelteKit, render(SvGrid, { props }) from svelte/server returns table markup with the data baked in, so the first paint carries real rows before hydration. The gallery has no server runtime, so this demo snapshots the client-rendered grid into a script-blocked iframe to show the shape of the markup without JavaScript; the real check is the pnpm ssr:check script against a server build.
keywords: sveltekit data grid server side rendering

faq.question: Does SvGrid render rows on the server?
faq.answer: Yes. Rendering the component on the server produces the table with header and data rows for the initial state, and the client hydrates it for interactivity.

faq.question: Why is this demo a snapshot instead of real SSR?
faq.answer: The demo gallery is a static site with no server. Capturing the client DOM and showing it in an iframe that blocks scripts demonstrates that the markup carries the data, but only a real server build can catch an SSR regression.

faq.question: What about virtualization on the server?
faq.answer: The server has no viewport, so the initial render emits the first window of rows; hydration takes over scrolling and renders the rest on demand.
